correctness.rationale: The exact graph definition and all-simple-hexagon domain are unambiguous. Two complete hexagon enumerations and an independent affine-configuration graph model agree on 24 cycles. Every signed quotient character is tested twice (direct sum and integer Walsh transform), with a nine-dimensional gauge reduction justified by cut-cycle orthogonality. The complete kernel coefficients sum in absolute value to 3936, proving norm 3936/512=123/16; character diagonalization establishes rank and condition number; translation averaging proves unrestricted endpoint optimality. No finite sample is extrapolated to an infinite claim.

value.rationale: Shortest cycles are an intrinsic orbit of a canonical cubic symmetric graph and form a natural codebook for measuring edge-bit signals. Exact cancellation determines identifiability; the signed spectrum, sharp surviving inverse norm and optimal endpoint projector norm are directly motivated recovery invariants, not recovered from a mere graph adjacency spectrum. The explicit nine-dimensional reduction and two-model certificate make the finite exact fact reusable for benchmarking cycle-code inverse problems; no larger unproved theorem is needed for this natural finite instance.
